attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - density separation at d50=10 µm in a hydrocyclone is physically impossible for organisms near water density (zooplankton, larvae, many protists have density ~1.01–1.05 g/cm³); the centrifugal settling velocity scales with (ρp−ρf) and at 10 µm the Stokes terminal velocity in the cyclone's effective g-field is orders of magnitude below what is needed to overcome fluid drag and turbulence, so the claimed d50 of 10 µm by density alone cannot hold.
attacks.weak_transfer: KILLED - the mechanism relies on inertial/density separation at low Reynolds number where the d50 is governed by particle-equivalent settling velocity, but the testable prediction specifies a 10 µm polystyrene sphere (ρ≈1.05 g/cm³) as proxy; polystyrene at 10 µm is the upper bound of what any realistic hydrocyclone can cut at this flow, and actual organisms with densities within 0.01 g/cm³ of seawater and often non-spherical/biologically active shapes will have drastically higher effective d50, invalidating the transfer from polystyrene challenge to biological claim.
